notes.title: Untangling the tangled.
notes.notes:
Hi again,

Another small update, this time we've moved some fixes for Borrack over to Tangled Tales, and fixed a bug that could make it impossible to remove objects from containers. Thankfully it was rare!

Enjoy.

notes.title: Small Patch
notes.notes:
Hi all,

We've made a few fixes and tweaks to The Eye of Borrack, fixing a rare occurrence, where the game couldn't be completed if you performed certain actions in a certain order.

Also added a few new commands, which don't affect game-play, but add a little more atmosphere.

notes.title: Forget me not.,
notes.notes:
Fixed small, and very rare bug that caused characters to forget what the wanted, making some puzzles impossible to solve.  Most players won't have encountered it, but if you did, you can now proceed.

Enjoy,

The JimJams Games team.

notes.title: The Adventures Continue
notes.notes:
[b]The Adventure Chronicles[/b]

We're excited to annouce that our first adventure collaboration bundle will release in 2 days.

The Adventure Chronicles is an amazing collection of some of the best classically-inspired text-based adventure games, all with a slightly modern twist.

Brought to you by some of the masters of the genre, the pack includes a redux based on the original [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1171560/Adventureland_XL/]Adventureland[/url] game created in 1978 by Scott Adams. A brand new adventure, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1170960/The_Eye_of_Borrack/]The Eye of Borrack[/url] from Dave Hawkins of JimJams Games, author of Stranded for the ZX Spectrum, (voted 31st best ZX Spectrum adventure game of all time by [url=https://worldofspectrum.net/archive/best-adventures/]WorldofSpectrum.net[/url] users.).

Added to this is the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/930630/The_Lost_Legends_of_Redwall_Escape_the_Gloomer/]"Lost Legends of Redwall: Escape the Gloomer"[/url] by Soma Games, an adventure based on Mossflower, one of the NYT bestselling Redwall™ books by Brian Jacques, which to date has sold over 35 million copies! If that's not enough, you'll find two new works from [url=https://store.steampowered.com/search/?publisher=Unimatrix+Productions]Unimatrix Productions[/url] that bring a modern slant to the genre, combining the best of interactive fiction, visual novels, and gamebooks.

notes.title: The Eye of Borrack - Tangled Tales
notes.notes: It's Christmas time, so as a thank you to all of our great players, we've added new DLC to The Eye of Borrack for free, giving you a brand new adventure set in the same mythical land. Play as either Cinderella or Prince Charming as you try to make your way back through a mysterious forest full of magical, and to be honest, fairly annoying fairy tale creatures.

notes.title: AgAIn
notes.notes:
Hi all,

We've released a small update today, improving the way the AI's navigate. It's mainly aimed at bringing our text adventures in-line with the latest features of our new in-house engine.

Enjoy,

The JimJams Games team.

notes.title: Saying more...
notes.notes:
Hi, fellow Adventurers.

We've another update for you, this time focusing on the AI.

We've once again listened to feedback, and improved the way you can talk to other characters in the game.

Expanding on our recent changes to the SAY command we've fixed a couple of small bugs that crept in when we updated SAY.

In addition, we've added the ability to give characters multiple commands, adding to the depth of puzzles and ease of play.

So, for example, CHIEF "TAKE THE BOX AND THE KEY", ASK RANDLE TO TAKE ALL. - NOTE: We've checked this system a lot, but please report any issues.

Secondly, we've also improved a few routes in the game following feedback, for example, where a fallen tree forms a bridge to the north, you can now CROSS TREE or CROSS BRIDGE as well as GO NORTH.

We've also added a new command SHOWINPUT which will toggle between showing the last typed command and not. Some users felt showing the last input was unnecessary as it's obvious from the response, while others liked it, so now you have the choice.

Lastly, we've now made it impossible to die. well, sort of. There has to be a penalty,  so death will now lead to a player respawn back in the hut and a loss of points. If you want the perfect score, best stay alive.

That's it,

As always, enjoy.

The JimJamsGames team.

notes.title: What did you SAY?
notes.notes:
Hi all,

A small update today for The Eye of Borrack, all based on user feedback.

1) We've improved SAY, so, as an example, you've always been able to SAY TO RANDLE "FOLLOW ME", now you can SAY "FOLLOW ME" to the world in general, and anyone who is around will listen (They might not do what you want, but they will listen.). - Of course, this can be used with other commands as well, so you could SAY "Hello" to the world, or SAY TO EVERYONE WAIT HERE.

2) We've added a new system command, SHOWINPUT which will toggle between displaying the last player input entered. Many players felt that there was no need to display what you'd just typed, so we removed it in a previous build.. This annoyed some players, so we've now given you a choice.

3) We also made a few tweaks to some locations and added a few improved ways to interact with certain objects, you most likely won't notice them, but will improve the user experience.

4) We've updated the manual to relect these changes.

That's it, enjoy,

The JimJams Games team.

notes.title: Big Improvements
notes.notes:
Hi text adventure fans.

Firstly, this patch corrects a few typos that were spotted by eagle-eyed players.

We've also added the new WINDOWED mode to the drop-down graphics menu for ease.

CHANGE: You can now add a save/load slot to SAVE (number) or LOAD (number) which will allow you to select a slot when saving/loading. NOTE: This won't change the default slot set by SAVESLOT

We've also brought the way The Eye of Borrack displays your last command in line with the upcoming Stranded 2 by removing the text showing what was last typed. It was causing confusion for some players and due to the way it was being decoded sometimes returned odd results, even though it was understood.

We've also improved the error reporting when a noun is known, but not understood in the current situation, making it easier to understand what was misunderstood.

We've updated the manual to reflect all of these changes, which we were told today by a very old hand to the text adventure scene, was "really retro" - so we must be doing something right.

There are a couple of other improvements behind the scenes that generally make things better!

That's all for now and as always.

Enjoy.

The JimJams Games team.

notes.title: Come and Chat with us.
notes.notes:
Hi all,

We get a lot of requests for help from our players who are stuck scratching their heads over a puzzle here and a puzzle there in The Eye of Borrack, so we're launching a discord chat channel where you can meet other players and occasionally chat with the devs. So, if you need help with the game, why not come and join us.

[url=https://discord.gg/9DXSWNT]Join us on Discord.[/url]

Looking forward to seeing you there,

The JimJams Games team.

notes.title: Small Patch Time!
notes.notes:
Hi all,

In keeping with our intention to update and improve on all of our games, even months and years after publication, we've taken a little time out to make some changes to the parsing system, bringing it in line with our next text adventure Stranded 2, which is well into development.

We hope that these changes improve your enjoyment of this already very popular game!

Thanks for playing,

The JimJams Games team.

notes.title: Better searching.
notes.notes:
Hi all,

This is a very small update, improving the parser when searching objects and we've added a save game warning now when quitting.

That's it.

Enjoy,

The JimJams Games team.

notes.title: New Views and Improvements.
notes.notes:
Hi all,

Firstly, many thanks to our players and the excellent feedback we've received from many of you. 

We're currently working on our next text adventure Stranded 2, which is a sequel to a game our lead developer wrote back in the early 1990's, for the amazing ZX Spectrum. Yep, he goes back a long way.

As a result, we've made some improvements to the main engine, mainly to parsing and object recognition for similar-sounding objects. (E.g. A red, metal key and a red, silver key.).

We've also added a much-requested Windows mode. You can now type WINDOWED ON or WINDOWED OFF to turn on a scalable Window, or simply WINDOWED to toggle between the two modes.

That's it, thanks for reading, and we hope you continue to enjoy The Eye of Borrack.

The JimJams Games team.

notes.title: Looking better!
notes.notes:
Hi all,

While we're busy behind the scenes working on a couple of other projects, including a sequel to The Eye of Borrack, we've taken time to pass some engine improvements for that sequel back to Borrack.

There are lots of little tweaks, but we've mainly improved the amount of information that examining or searching an object or location reveals, giving the player more to work with, and the occasional clue.

Thanks all,

Enjoy,

The JimJams Games team

notes.title: It's nomination time!
notes.notes:
Hi All,

So, it seems that some kind people have nominated The Eye of Borrack for the most Most Innovative Gameplay award here on Steam. We're amazed and very happy for the honour. 

We're committed to bringing you fun, challenging games, which stretch your playing skills. Please help us get a little more recognition, by voting for us too. 

Many thanks,

The JimJams Games team.

notes.title: Autumn Sale is here.
notes.notes:
Hi all,

It's that time of year again, and we're pleased to let you know that The Eye of Borrack, our take on the classic text-adventure is available for a short time at 33% off.

So, grab a copy of some truely retro gaming now.

Enjoy,

The JimJams Games team.

notes.title: Ah, now I understand.....
notes.notes:
Hi,

We've published another small update. While working on a sequel to the Eye of Borrack, we discovered a few areas where the parser can better predict what the player means.

In our constant search for excellence, we've ported those improvements back into Borrack, so all of our games will have the best parsing we can manage.

Thanks all,

The JimJams Games team.

notes.title: Better thinking.
notes.notes:
HI all,

Another small update today. I imagine that this will be the last for a little while.

We've been following feedback closely and thought that the AI could a little better behaved. So, on top of the recent AI updates,  We've improved how the AI handle objects further, and also given them a little more personality.

Thanks all.

The JimJams Games team.

notes.title: Little Thieves
notes.notes:
Hi all,

Once again, we've reacted to player feedback. This time regarding some light-fingered characters.

It appears that a few characters have been taking objects, and holding onto them for far too long, or dropping them far from the original location. This was intended behaviour in a way, but not very helpful.

Characters will drop items pretty quickly now if they've taken them, been given them or otherwise are in possession unless it's something that they really like.

Thanks for all your support,

The JimJams Games team.

notes.title: Lighting the Way
notes.notes:
Hi all,

We've been collecting feedback from our players, most of which is great, so we're very happy that you like what we're doing.

Some of you thought that the torch could be easy to use, and we agreed.

So, what's new.

1) The Torch can now be refilled, even when not empty,

2) You can now light the torch, even in the dark.

3) You can now empty the torch, simply because you should be able to.

In non-torch related news, we've fixed a few more typos. There haven't been many, but they do creep in, and we're keen to eliminate them all!

We've also updated the end game music, to something much more dramatic.

That's it,

Enjoy,

The JimJams Games team.

notes.title: Take what?
notes.notes:
Hi all,

Another quick update today. We hadn't intended to update quite like this, but our great players are full of ideas.

Firstly, we've made it simpler to take objects from containers.

Providing you know that an object is in a container, and of course, it's present, you'll now be able to use TAKE [object], and the parser will attempt to guess the location.

So, if the sword was in the chest, and you'd seen it there, you could

TAKE THE SWORD FROM THE CHEST
TAKE SWORD (and the parser will fill in the rest.).

Of course, the normal rules apply, the chest must be open, unlocked and of here, etc.

Secondly, we've tweaked a few more commands, to widen the sentence structure you can use. E.g. SET can now be used to SET DIAL, SET FIRE and SET DOWN THE SWORD.

And lastly, we're still tackling the bugbear of small typos, which we're fixing as soon as we spot them or they are reported.

That's it for now,

Many thanks,

The JimJams Games team.

notes.title: Read all about it!
notes.notes:
Hi all,

A little bit of news today.

We were very pleased to have been recently interviewed for The Classic Adventurer Magazine. An online and physical volume dedicated to all things text adventure and interactive fiction.

You can read a very in-depth article on JimJams Games and the history of our lead developer, Dave Hawkins.

[url=http://classicadventurer.co.uk/]Classic Adventurer Issue 6[/url]

Enjoy,

The JimJams Games team.

notes.title: Quick Fix
notes.notes:
Hi all,

A quick fix tonight. Mostly to fix typos, but also to fix a bug that was causing Oops to misbehave.  

That's it, 

Thanks for playing,

The JimJams Games team.

notes.title: Another day in Paradise
notes.notes:
Hi all,

There's a small update to The Eye of Borrack.

Following feedback from a few users, we've fixed some typos, mostly caused by some code generated text, and a few in the manual, that were caused by a tired author.

We've also added the ability to load your last saved game on launch for quick access. If you're running a new game, you'll need to load your old game manually as normal on the first run of this build. The last saved game slot is recorded on QUIT.

Lastly, we've improved some of the puzzle text a little to make the results of the players' actions slightly clearer.

That's it for now, we did say it was a small update.

Thanks all,

The JimJams Games team.

notes.title: We're live!
notes.notes:
Hi all,

We're pleased to announce that The Eye of Borrack has been released into the wide world today. Our take on the text-adventure genre challenges the player to explore a wild, magical world as they seek to unlock the mystery of Borrack.

We've gone truly old-school with this release, with a game that can trace its roots back to the 1970s.  You use English phrases and sentences to communicate with the game and to manipulate objects and characters as you battle to solve the many puzzles before you.

Enjoy the Eye of Borrack all, and as always, we'll be updating based on feedback, so expect the game to evolve.

Thanks,

The JimJams Games team.

notes.title: The Eye of Borrack
notes.notes:
Hi all,

Here at JimJams Games, we're truly going retro with our latest release, This time, we're moving away from our normal shooters and we've decided to focus on a classic text-based puzzler. We're still tweaking, but fans of interactive fiction can grab themselves a copy from 22nd October 2019.

We've thought long and hard about this one, and have been working alongside some giants of the genre to bring you a humourous, challenging, text puzzler, with a very retro feel.

If you've not tried a text adventure, this is your chance to delve into the amazingly fun, immersive world of interactive fiction, where your actions are defined not by single keypresses, or controllers, but by entering English sentences to guide your character on a strange and fantastic journey.

More to come as we near the 22nd October 2019.

The JimJams Games team.
